faq.q: Can I change a jewelry photo background and lighting?
faq.a: Yes. Remove the old background and choose new lighting or a simple scene. You can make several looks without another photo shoot.

faq.q: How do I keep stones and clasps accurate?
faq.a: Use a sharp photo and compare the result with the real piece. Make another version if a stone, clasp, or color changes.

faq.q: Can I make jewelry photos without a person?
faq.a: Yes. Choose a simple table or studio scene for the piece. You can change the background without hiring a model.

faq.q: How do I check an AI jewelry photo before posting?
faq.a: Compare it with your real jewelry at full size. Check stones, clasps, links, and color so shoppers see the piece you sell.

faq.q: How much does a jewelry photo cost?
faq.a: Each photo costs 24 credits. Starter costs $24.50 a month for 200 credits, Pro costs $35 for 300, and Premium costs $63 for 600.

faq.q: Do I need to hire a jewelry model?
faq.a: No. You can show your jewelry on a digital person from your product photo. Check the fit and product details before using the image.

faq.q: Can AI show how a necklace looks when worn?
faq.a: Yes. Use a clear necklace photo to make an image showing it on a person. Check that the length and details match your product.

faq.q: What photo should I upload for jewelry images?
faq.a: Upload a sharp photo of the whole piece on a plain surface. Show the clasp, stones, chain, and any details customers need to see.

faq.q: Can I try one jewelry piece before making more photos?
faq.a: Yes. Start with one clear photo and check the result before making images for the rest of your catalog.

faq.q: Which jewelry pieces can appear on a person?
faq.a: You can show necklaces, earrings, rings, bracelets, and cufflinks on a person. Check each image against the real piece before posting.

steps.prompt: Show an adult wearing the silver necklace at the collarbone, with a light touch on the chain so the size is easy to judge. Keep the pendant and chain visible, in soft window light.

reviews.h2: How Jewelry Sellers Edit the Tray
reviews.lead: Four sellers start from one piece photo, clear the cloth, and keep the metal they shot.

items.t: Keep the Stones and the Crop
items.d: They clear the cloth under a stone necklace and run that same crop on the next chain. They check every stone against the photo they took.
They take pins and the grey cloth off a stud photo, then add a soft shadow under the metal. The color stays the one they shot.
They center a size run on the same point of the square. The next size uses that crop instead of a new table setup.
They change only the area around an old locket and read the engraving against the source. The file stays off the site if a prong moved.
